After analyzing the position, I found the clearly best move using systematic forcing-line analysis.

**Best move:** Nc5

**Main line:** Nc5 Nc3+ Kf3 Bxe3 Bxe3 

This centralizing knight move creates a **fork**, simultaneously attacking the undefended pawns on a6 and b7. Black must respond to these dual threats. If Black tries to create counterplay with Nc3+ (check), White moves the king to f3. Black's last resort—capturing on e3 with the bishop—fails because White recaptures with the bishop and wins material (bishop + pawn for pawn, netting +2 for White). The knight on c5 dominates, leaving Black's position untenable. 

**Key lesson:** When your opponent makes an attacking move like Bh6, look for centralizing knight moves that create multiple threats. A well-placed knight can outweigh active opponent pieces.
